Translate platform identity into application-specific access and accountability.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Application users, roles, privileges and user-role links.
  • Consumes Security account events to maintain app-local users.
  • Usage analysis and cleanup when an application is deleted.

Why the boundary matters

An authenticated person is not automatically authorised everywhere; application permissions stay explicit and locally owned.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.AppSecurity on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.AppSecurity" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddAppSecurityWeb(/* platform configuration */);
app.StartAppSecurityWeb();

Configure and run it

The host needs Core data access, Security identity, Eventing and the App Security API route. A background-only process can use AddAppSecurityHostedServices and StartAppSecurityHostedServices.

Consume the capability

Use the App, User, Role, Privilege and UserRole endpoints. Let the supplied event handlers create and clean application-local security state when identities or apps change.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.AppSecurity.git
cd cCoder.AppSecurity
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
